text: So the first question was, and the one that I think is on everybody's mind right at the moment, is there is a bunch of questions related to COVID-19, the vaccination rollout updates, priorities and scheduling, how the municipalities can help, an update on when restrictions might or could be lifted, impact on mental health and provincial support for that, a roadmap out of a roadmap out of lockdown restrictions and support arrangements available to small, medium businesses during the lockdown were all topics that were raised by Council. speaker: bradrutherford
text: I will try to cover off all of that. And if I miss something, just let me know. The vaccination rollout obviously was interrupted by supply as we got into the end of January. For most of February, we were where the province was able to administer second doses only. And as they were trying to go through their rollout program, which is has the phase one, it's broken into two different parts, but they're in phase one still. We are expecting that we're going to have some more consistent supply coming up, but still reduce numbers. And the federal government is still talking about meeting the contractual responsibilities from Pfizer and Moderna by the end of March. We should see this week a much bigger allocation of both of Pfizer and then followed by Moderna, which is coming every couple of weeks, I think three weeks actually on that cycle. And in terms of what the municipalities can do, I know that the province is at a point where they are able to administer far more doses than what they have. Where the municipalities are going to fit in specifically, I think that'll be up to Alberta Health and the Health Ministry, or possibly PIC, which is the cabinet committee to come up with that kind of plan. I think they're going to use pharmacists as an example as we get into later stages, as well to help that rollout. The volume is probably going to increase as we get through to the end of February into March. And the province has let us know that they're ready for that volume increase. And I think they're going to be able to administer vaccines quite quickly, making sure that they're hitting those targeted groups in phase one, 1A and 1B, and then starting to work through the next phases. So phase two, cabinet has not brought out who is included in phase two yet. I imagine they'll do that shortly. But I think the overarching concern is just a steady supply, which helps in the planning, and then getting those doses administered as well. In terms of supports, there was a $5,000 relaunch grant that came up several months ago. An additional $15,000 was added by the province. There's been some clarity and some reworking of federal programs around rental assistance as well to help businesses. I have and will continue to maintain the same open question to people in the business community as to where the supports fall short. Is there any gaps where people are not able to access the funds? We've come up, there's been a few examples of still those gaps existing, and trying to help people with the application and into the ministry as well to get answers back. Some of them have been quick and getting things done within a couple days. Others have been a bit slower. I know that for a lot of these businesses, what they're going to be looking for is the ability to really get a fair chance at just being able to operate and to be able to generate the revenue that they were generating before. The heaviest restrictions are on about 1% of businesses. Then there's other restrictions in the broader group. It still affects a lot of people. This pandemic has affected a lot of people in a variety of ways. It's not lost on the government that additional supports may be necessary. I leave that to the government to announce and to deal with as we go into the future. For me, the feedback that helps is where does it fall short and how can we close any gaps or loopholes that are existing so that businesses that are affected are able to get that support as well. Martin, can you just remind me of a couple of the other questions? Impacts on mental health and provincial support. On mental health, there was $53 million allocated for mental health. There was a few Beaumont locations and Leduc locations that received some funding. That was throughout different communities. One was a church in Beaumont and one was in Leduc that received some funding to help with mental health and to make sure that there was additional supports for folks. This has been ongoing. That happened early on. They realized how necessary this is. It's really incumbent upon all of us to be reaching out to one another and to people who may need some support and to encourage that they reach out for assistance as well and really touch base with one another. What I get from phone calls in the last week or two is that there's a growing fatigue with restrictions and people are feeling frustrated. I think it's probably a natural response to what's happening. There's a lot of stress around this and it's been prolonged as well. We didn't come right out of a boom into something like this. There's been struggles for a number of years. We're hit with this and there's three aspects that really affect people. You have the energy price collapse, global recession and restrictions on a variety of businesses within our own province. There's a lot happening at once. When it comes to the phased plan, it's four phases. Some of the biggest changes occurred several weeks ago with schools going back in. That's around 700,000 students. Personal services by appointment were opened up like salons. Then we got to February 8th where restaurants and some of the other aspects of indoor fitness were relaxed as well. They put a three-week parameter in between each step, including other metrics like hospitalization, just to see how each step is going to affect the case rate. For the February 8th changes, I think it takes a week to 10 days before you start seeing it in the numbers as to what effect it may or may not have and how it's doing.
